title: Java Programming Mastery
subtitle: Complete Guide from Beginner to Advanced
author: Programming Experts

chapters.title: Introduction to Java
chapters.description: Understanding Java programming language and its importance

pages.title: What is Java?
pages.content: Java is a high-level, object-oriented programming language developed by Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle). It is widely used for building web applications, mobile apps, enterprise software, and Android applications.

quiz.question: Who developed Java?
quiz.explanation: Java was developed by Sun Microsystems.

pages.title: Features of Java
pages.content: Java offers several powerful features including platform independence, object-oriented programming, strong security, and automatic memory management.
pages.exampleCode: System.out.println("Java is platform independent");

quiz.question: What does WORA stand for in Java?
quiz.explanation: WORA means Write Once Run Anywhere.

pages.title: Java Architecture
pages.content: Java programs are compiled into bytecode which runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). This architecture allows Java programs to run on any system with a JVM installed.

quiz.question: What runs Java bytecode?
quiz.explanation: Java bytecode runs on the Java Virtual Machine.

pages.title: Installing Java (JDK)
pages.content: To run Java programs, you need to install the Java Development Kit (JDK). The JDK includes the compiler (javac) and runtime environment required to build and execute Java applications.
pages.exampleCode: java -version

quiz.question: Which package contains the Java compiler?
quiz.explanation: The Java Development Kit (JDK) contains the Java compiler.

pages.title: First Java Program
pages.content: Every Java application starts from the main method. The main method is the entry point of a Java program.

quiz.question: Which method is the entry point of a Java program?
quiz.explanation: main() is the starting point of a Java program.

chapters.title: Variables and Data Types
chapters.description: Understanding how Java stores and manages different types of data

pages.title: Introduction to Variables
pages.content: Variables are containers used to store data values. In Java, every variable must have a data type that defines the kind of data it can store.
keyPoints: Variable name should follow naming rules
Variables must be initialized before use

quiz.question: What is a variable in Java?
quiz.explanation: A variable is used to store data values in Java.

pages.title: Variable Naming Rules
pages.content: Java variables must follow specific naming rules. A variable name can start with a letter, underscore, or dollar sign but cannot start with a number.
pages.exampleCode:
int studentAge = 20;
String studentName = "Alice";
keyPoints: Must start with letter, underscore, or dollar sign

quiz.question: Which of the following is a valid variable name?
quiz.explanation: student_age is a valid variable name.

pages.title: Primitive Data Types
pages.content: Java provides primitive data types which store simple values such as numbers and characters. These include int, float, double, char, and boolean.
keyPoints: Primitive data types store simple values

quiz.question: Which data type stores a single character?
quiz.explanation: char stores a single character value.

pages.title: Non-Primitive Data Types
pages.content: Non-primitive data types refer to objects and references. These include classes, arrays, and strings.
pages.exampleCode:
String name = "Java";
int[] numbers = {1,2,3,4};
keyPoints: Examples include String, Array, and Class

quiz.question: Which of the following is a non-primitive data type?
quiz.explanation: String is a non-primitive data type.

pages.title: Type Casting
pages.content: Type casting is the process of converting one data type into another. Java supports two types of casting: implicit and explicit casting.

quiz.question: Which type casting happens automatically?
quiz.explanation: Implicit casting happens automatically.

pages.title: Constants
pages.content: Constants are variables whose values cannot be changed once assigned. In Java, constants are declared using the final keyword.
pages.exampleCode:
final double PI = 3.14159;
System.out.println(PI);

quiz.question: Which keyword defines a constant in Java?
quiz.explanation: The final keyword is used to define constants.

chapters.title: Operators
chapters.description: Understanding different types of operators used in Java programming

pages.title: Introduction to Operators
pages.content: Operators in Java are special symbols used to perform operations on variables and values. They are used to manipulate data and perform calculations in programs.

quiz.question: What are operators used for?
quiz.explanation: Operators perform operations on variables and values.

pages.title: Arithmetic Operators
pages.content: Arithmetic operators are used to perform mathematical operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.

quiz.question: Which operator gives the remainder?
quiz.explanation: The % operator returns the remainder.

pages.title: Relational Operators
pages.content: Relational operators compare two values and return a boolean result (true or false).

quiz.question: Which operator checks equality?
quiz.explanation: == is used to compare equality.

pages.title: Logical Operators
pages.content: Logical operators are used to combine multiple conditions and return boolean values.

quiz.question: Which operator represents Logical AND?
quiz.explanation: && is the logical AND operator.

pages.title: Assignment Operators
pages.content: Assignment operators are used to assign values to variables and sometimes combine operations with assignment.

quiz.question: Which operator adds a value and assigns it?
quiz.explanation: += adds a value and assigns it.

pages.title: Bitwise Operators
pages.content: Bitwise operators perform operations on binary values at the bit level. They are commonly used in low-level programming.

quiz.question: Which operator represents Bitwise OR?
quiz.explanation: | is the Bitwise OR operator.

chapters.title: Conditional Statements
chapters.description: Understanding decision-making statements in Java such as if, else, and switch

pages.title: Introduction to Conditional Statements
pages.content: Conditional statements allow programs to make decisions based on certain conditions. They help control the flow of execution depending on whether a condition is true or false.
keyPoints: Common statements include if, else, and switch

quiz.question: What is the purpose of conditional statements?
quiz.explanation: Conditional statements allow programs to make decisions based on conditions.

pages.title: if Statement
pages.content: The if statement executes a block of code only if the specified condition evaluates to true.

quiz.question: When does an if statement execute?
quiz.explanation: The if block executes only when the condition is true.

pages.title: if-else Statement
pages.content: The if-else statement allows executing one block of code if the condition is true and another block if the condition is false.
keyPoints: One block runs when condition is true
Another block runs when condition is false

quiz.question: Which block runs when the condition is false?
quiz.explanation: The else block runs when the condition is false.

pages.title: if-else-if Ladder
pages.content: The if-else-if ladder allows checking multiple conditions. The program executes the first block whose condition is true.

quiz.question: What happens when multiple conditions exist?
quiz.explanation: In an if-else-if ladder, the first true condition executes.

pages.title: Switch Statement
pages.content: The switch statement allows selecting one of many code blocks to execute based on the value of a variable.

quiz.question: Which keyword stops switch execution?
quiz.explanation: break stops further execution of switch cases.

pages.title: Switch vs If Statement
pages.content: Both switch and if statements control program flow. If statements are better for complex conditions, while switch works well for fixed values.

quiz.question: Which statement is better for many fixed values?
quiz.explanation: Switch works best when checking multiple fixed values.

chapters.title: Loops
chapters.description: Understanding loops in Java including for, while, do-while, break, and continue statements

pages.title: Introduction to Loops
pages.content: Loops allow a block of code to execute multiple times. They are useful when performing repetitive tasks such as iterating through numbers or collections.
keyPoints: Common loops include for, while, and do-while

quiz.question: What is the purpose of loops?
quiz.explanation: Loops repeat a block of code multiple times.

pages.title: For Loop
pages.content: The for loop is used when the number of iterations is known. It consists of initialization, condition, and increment/decrement.
keyPoints: Used when iteration count is known

quiz.question: Which loop is commonly used when the number of iterations is known?
quiz.explanation: The for loop is used when the number of iterations is known.

pages.title: While Loop
pages.content: The while loop executes a block of code as long as the specified condition remains true. It is commonly used when the number of iterations is not known in advance.
keyPoints: Useful when iteration count is unknown

quiz.question: When is a while loop useful?
quiz.explanation: While loops are useful when the number of iterations is unknown.

pages.title: Do-While Loop
pages.content: The do-while loop executes the block of code at least once before checking the condition. After execution, the condition is evaluated.
keyPoints: Useful when code must run at least once

quiz.question: Which loop guarantees at least one execution?
quiz.explanation: The do-while loop executes at least once.

pages.title: Break Statement
pages.content: The break statement immediately terminates the loop and transfers control to the next statement after the loop.
keyPoints: Used inside loops and switch statements

quiz.question: What does the break statement do?
quiz.explanation: The break statement stops loop execution.

pages.title: Continue Statement
pages.content: The continue statement skips the current iteration of the loop and moves to the next iteration.

quiz.question: What does the continue statement do?
quiz.explanation: Continue skips the current iteration and continues the loop.

chapters.title: Java Strings
chapters.description: Understanding String handling and operations in Java

pages.title: Introduction to Strings
pages.content: A String in Java is a sequence of characters used to represent text. Strings are widely used in programs for storing names, messages, and other textual data.
pages.exampleCode:
String name = "Java";
System.out.println(name);

quiz.question: What does a String store in Java?
quiz.explanation: Strings store characters and textual data.

pages.title: Creating Strings
pages.content: Strings in Java can be created in two ways: using string literals or using the new keyword with the String class.
keyPoints: String literals are stored in string pool

quiz.question: Which keyword creates a new String object?
quiz.explanation: The new keyword creates a new String object.

pages.title: Common String Methods
pages.content: Java provides many built-in methods to manipulate strings such as length(), toUpperCase(), toLowerCase(), and charAt().

quiz.question: Which method returns the length of a string?
quiz.explanation: length() returns the number of characters in a string.

pages.title: String Concatenation
pages.content: String concatenation combines two or more strings together. In Java, this is commonly done using the + operator or the concat() method.

quiz.question: Which operator joins two strings?
quiz.explanation: The + operator joins two strings.

pages.title: String Comparison
pages.content: Strings can be compared using the equals() method or compareTo() method. The == operator checks reference equality, not content equality.

quiz.question: Which method compares string content?
quiz.explanation: equals() compares the content of strings.

pages.title: StringBuilder
pages.content: StringBuilder is used when strings need to be modified frequently. Unlike String, StringBuilder objects are mutable, meaning their content can be changed.
keyPoints: append() adds text to existing string

quiz.question: Which class allows modifying strings efficiently?
quiz.explanation: StringBuilder allows modifying string content efficiently.

chapters.title: Arrays
chapters.description: Understanding arrays and how to store multiple values in Java

pages.title: Introduction to Arrays
pages.content: An array in Java is a collection of elements of the same data type stored in contiguous memory locations. Arrays allow storing multiple values in a single variable.
pages.exampleCode:
int[] numbers = {1,2,3,4,5};
System.out.println(numbers[0]);
keyPoints: Elements must be of the same type
Array elements are accessed using indexes

quiz.question: What does an array store?
quiz.explanation: Arrays store multiple values of the same data type.

pages.title: Declaring and Initializing Arrays
pages.content: Arrays can be declared and initialized in Java using square brackets []. They can also be initialized with values at the time of declaration.
keyPoints: Size must be defined when creating array
Values can be assigned later or during declaration

quiz.question: Which symbol is used to declare arrays?
quiz.explanation: Arrays are declared using square brackets [].

pages.title: Accessing Array Elements
pages.content: Array elements are accessed using their index number. In Java, array indexing starts from 0.

quiz.question: What is the index of the first element in Java arrays?
quiz.explanation: Java arrays start indexing from 0.

pages.title: Looping Through Arrays
pages.content: Loops can be used to iterate through array elements. The for loop is commonly used for this purpose.
keyPoints: Use loops to access all elements

quiz.question: Which property gives array length?
quiz.explanation: length returns the size of the array.

pages.title: Multidimensional Arrays
pages.content: Multidimensional arrays are arrays of arrays. They are commonly used to represent tables or matrices.

quiz.question: How do you access elements in a 2D array?
quiz.explanation: 2D arrays require two indexes to access elements.

pages.title: Enhanced For Loop
pages.content: Java provides an enhanced for loop (for-each loop) to iterate through arrays easily without using indexes.

quiz.question: Which loop simplifies iterating arrays?
quiz.explanation: The enhanced for loop simplifies array iteration.

chapters.title: Methods
chapters.description: Understanding methods in Java and how they help organize reusable code

pages.title: Introduction to Methods
pages.content: A method in Java is a block of code that performs a specific task. Methods help organize programs into smaller, reusable units.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of a method?
quiz.explanation: Methods perform specific tasks in programs.

pages.title: Method Syntax
pages.content: A method in Java consists of an access modifier, return type, method name, parameters, and a method body.

quiz.question: Which part defines the method name?
quiz.explanation: The method name identifies the method.

pages.title: Method Parameters
pages.content: Parameters allow methods to receive input values. These values are used inside the method to perform operations.

quiz.question: What are parameters used for?
quiz.explanation: Parameters allow passing values to methods.

pages.title: Return Values
pages.content: Methods can return values using the return keyword. The return type specifies what type of value the method returns.

quiz.question: Which keyword returns a value from a method?
quiz.explanation: The return keyword sends values from methods.

pages.title: Method Overloading
pages.content: Method overloading allows multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists. It improves code readability and flexibility.

quiz.question: What is method overloading?
options: Same method name with different parameters
quiz.explanation: Method overloading uses the same method name with different parameters.

pages.title: Recursion
pages.content: Recursion is a technique where a method calls itself to solve a problem. It is commonly used for problems like factorial calculation and tree traversal.

quiz.question: What is recursion?
quiz.explanation: Recursion occurs when a method calls itself.

chapters.title: Classes and Objects
chapters.description: Understanding how Java uses classes and objects in Object-Oriented Programming

pages.title: Introduction to Classes
pages.content: A class in Java is a blueprint used to create objects. It defines properties (variables) and behaviors (methods) that objects will have.
keyPoints: Class is a blueprint for objects

quiz.question: What is a class?
quiz.explanation: A class is a blueprint used to create objects.

pages.title: Objects in Java
pages.content: An object is an instance of a class. Objects allow accessing properties and methods defined in the class.
keyPoints: Object is an instance of a class

quiz.question: What creates an object in Java?
quiz.explanation: Objects are created using the new keyword.

pages.title: Constructors
pages.content: Constructors are special methods used to initialize objects. They have the same name as the class and are automatically called when an object is created.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of constructors?
quiz.explanation: Constructors initialize objects.

pages.title: Access Modifiers
pages.content: Access modifiers control the visibility of classes, variables, and methods in Java. Common modifiers include public, private, and protected.

quiz.question: Which modifier restricts access within the class only?
quiz.explanation: Private restricts access within the class.

pages.title: this Keyword
pages.content: The this keyword refers to the current object. It is commonly used to differentiate instance variables from parameters.

quiz.question: What does the this keyword refer to?
quiz.explanation: this refers to the current object.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.description: Understanding how inheritance allows classes to reuse code in Java

pages.title: Introduction to Inheritance
pages.content: Inheritance allows one class to inherit properties and methods from another class. It promotes code reuse and establishes relationships between classes.
keyPoints: Child class inherits from parent class

quiz.question: What is inheritance used for?
quiz.explanation: Inheritance promotes code reuse.

pages.title: Extending a Class
pages.content: Inheritance in Java is implemented using the extends keyword. The child class inherits properties and methods from the parent class.

quiz.question: Which keyword is used for inheritance?
quiz.explanation: The extends keyword is used for inheritance.

pages.title: Types of Inheritance
pages.content: Java supports several types of inheritance including single, multilevel, and hierarchical inheritance.

quiz.question: Which inheritance type involves multiple levels?
quiz.explanation: Multilevel inheritance involves multiple levels.

pages.title: super Keyword
pages.content: The super keyword refers to the parent class. It is used to access parent class methods and constructors.

quiz.question: What does the super keyword refer to?
quiz.explanation: super refers to the parent class.

pages.title: Method Overriding
pages.content: Method overriding allows a subclass to provide a specific implementation of a method that is already defined in its parent class.

quiz.question: What does method overriding do?
quiz.explanation: Method overriding changes parent class method behavior.

chapters.title: Polymorphism and Abstraction
chapters.description: Understanding polymorphism and abstraction concepts in Java Object-Oriented Programming

pages.title: Introduction to Polymorphism
pages.content: Polymorphism in Java means 'many forms'. It allows methods to behave differently depending on the object calling them.
keyPoints: Allows same method name with different behavior

quiz.question: What does polymorphism mean?
quiz.explanation: Polymorphism means many forms or behaviors.

pages.title: Method Overloading
pages.content: Method overloading allows multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists within the same class.

quiz.question: What defines method overloading?
quiz.explanation: Method overloading requires same name but different parameters.

pages.title: Method Overriding
pages.content: Method overriding occurs when a subclass provides its own implementation of a method already defined in the parent class.

quiz.question: What type of polymorphism is method overriding?
quiz.explanation: Method overriding occurs at runtime.

pages.title: Introduction to Abstraction
pages.content: Abstraction hides implementation details and only shows essential features of an object. It helps reduce complexity and increase security.

quiz.question: What does abstraction hide?
quiz.explanation: Abstraction hides internal implementation details.

pages.title: Abstract Classes
pages.content: Abstract classes are classes that cannot be instantiated and may contain abstract methods that must be implemented by subclasses.
keyPoints: Cannot create objects of abstract class
Must be extended by child classes

quiz.question: Can we create objects of an abstract class?
quiz.explanation: Abstract classes cannot be instantiated.

pages.title: Interfaces
pages.content: Interfaces define a contract that classes must implement. They allow multiple inheritance in Java and help achieve abstraction.

quiz.question: Which keyword is used to implement an interface?
quiz.explanation: Classes use the implements keyword to implement interfaces.

chapters.title: Exception Handling
chapters.description: Understanding how Java handles runtime errors using exception handling mechanisms

pages.title: Introduction to Exceptions
pages.content: An exception is an unexpected event that occurs during program execution and disrupts the normal flow of the program.
keyPoints: Java provides mechanisms to handle errors

quiz.question: What is an exception?
quiz.explanation: Exceptions occur during runtime execution.

pages.title: Try-Catch Block
pages.content: The try-catch block is used to handle exceptions. The try block contains code that may cause an exception, and the catch block handles the exception.

quiz.question: Which block handles exceptions?
quiz.explanation: The catch block handles exceptions.

pages.title: Finally Block
pages.content: The finally block always executes regardless of whether an exception occurs or not. It is commonly used for closing resources.

quiz.question: Which block always executes?
quiz.explanation: The finally block always executes.

pages.title: Throw Keyword
pages.content: The throw keyword is used to explicitly throw an exception in Java.
pages.exampleCode: throw new ArithmeticException("Division by zero");

quiz.question: Which keyword throws an exception?
quiz.explanation: The throw keyword is used to throw exceptions.

pages.title: Throws Keyword
pages.content: The throws keyword declares exceptions that a method may generate. It informs the caller that the method may throw exceptions.

quiz.question: Where is the throws keyword used?
quiz.explanation: Throws is used in method declaration.

pages.title: Custom Exceptions
pages.content: Custom exceptions allow developers to create their own exception classes to handle specific errors.

quiz.question: Which class is extended to create custom exceptions?
quiz.explanation: Custom exceptions extend the Exception class.

chapters.title: Collections Framework
chapters.description: Understanding Java Collections used to store and manipulate groups of objects

pages.title: Introduction to Collections
pages.content: The Java Collections Framework provides classes and interfaces to store and manipulate groups of objects efficiently.
pages.exampleCode:
import java.util.ArrayList;

ArrayList<String> list = new ArrayList<>();

quiz.question: Which package contains collections?
quiz.explanation: Collections are part of java.util package.

pages.title: List Interface
pages.content: The List interface stores ordered collections that allow duplicate elements.
pages.exampleCode:
List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
names.add("Java");

quiz.question: Does List allow duplicate values?
quiz.explanation: Lists allow duplicate elements.

pages.title: Set Interface
pages.content: The Set interface stores unique elements and does not allow duplicates.
pages.exampleCode:
Set<Integer> numbers = new HashSet<>();
numbers.add(1);

quiz.question: Which collection does not allow duplicates?
quiz.explanation: Set does not allow duplicate elements.

pages.title: Map Interface
pages.content: The Map interface stores key-value pairs where each key maps to a specific value.
pages.exampleCode:
Map<Integer,String> map = new HashMap<>();
map.put(1,"Java");

quiz.question: What does Map store?
quiz.explanation: Map stores key-value pairs.

pages.title: ArrayList
pages.content: ArrayList is a resizable array implementation of the List interface.
pages.exampleCode:
ArrayList<String> list = new ArrayList<>();
list.add("Java");

quiz.question: Which collection is a dynamic array?
quiz.explanation: ArrayList is a dynamic array implementation.

pages.title: HashMap
pages.content: HashMap stores key-value pairs and allows fast data retrieval using keys.
pages.exampleCode:
HashMap<Integer,String> map = new HashMap<>();
map.put(1,"Java");

quiz.question: Which collection stores key-value pairs?
quiz.explanation: HashMap stores key-value pairs.

chapters.title: File Handling
chapters.description: Understanding how Java reads and writes files using File, FileReader, and FileWriter classes

pages.title: Introduction to File Handling
pages.content: File handling in Java allows programs to create, read, write, and delete files. It helps store data permanently outside the program.
pages.exampleCode:
import java.io.File;

File file = new File("example.txt");

quiz.question: Which package is used for file handling in Java?
quiz.explanation: The java.io package provides classes for file handling.

pages.title: Creating a File
pages.content: Java provides the File class to create files. The createNewFile() method is used to create a new file.
keyPoints: File must be handled using exceptions

quiz.question: Which method creates a new file?
quiz.explanation: createNewFile() creates a new file.

pages.title: Writing to Files
pages.content: Java allows writing data to files using classes like FileWriter and BufferedWriter.

quiz.question: Which class is used to write data into files?
quiz.explanation: FileWriter writes data to files.

pages.title: Reading Files
pages.content: Java reads files using FileReader, BufferedReader, or Scanner classes.

quiz.question: Which class reads file data?
quiz.explanation: FileReader reads data from files.

pages.title: BufferedReader and BufferedWriter
pages.content: BufferedReader and BufferedWriter improve file reading and writing performance by buffering data.

quiz.question: Which class reads file line by line?
quiz.explanation: BufferedReader reads file content line by line.

pages.title: Deleting Files
pages.content: Java allows deleting files using the delete() method from the File class.
pages.exampleCode:
File file = new File("test.txt");
file.delete();

quiz.question: Which method deletes a file?
quiz.explanation: delete() removes a file.

chapters.title: Java Mini Projects
chapters.description: Applying Java concepts through small practical projects

pages.title: Calculator Application
pages.content: This project creates a simple calculator that performs basic arithmetic operations like addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.

quiz.question: Which class is used to take input in Java?
quiz.explanation: Scanner is used to take user input in Java.

pages.title: Student Management System
pages.content: This project stores student details such as name and marks and displays them using classes and objects.

quiz.question: Which concept stores student data here?
quiz.explanation: Classes and objects are used to store student data.

pages.title: Number Guessing Game
pages.content: This game generates a random number and asks the user to guess it. The program provides feedback if the guess is correct or incorrect.

quiz.question: Which class generates random numbers?
quiz.explanation: Random class generates random numbers.

pages.title: File Organizer
pages.content: This project organizes files in directories using Java file handling. It demonstrates reading and managing files.

quiz.question: Which class manages files?
quiz.explanation: File class manages file operations.

pages.title: Simple Banking System
pages.content: This project simulates a basic banking system with deposit and withdraw operations using classes and methods.

quiz.question: Which concept is used in banking system project?
quiz.explanation: The banking system uses object-oriented programming.

pages.title: API Data Fetching
pages.content: Java applications can connect to APIs to retrieve data from the internet. This project demonstrates basic API communication.

quiz.question: Which package helps connect to web APIs?
quiz.explanation: java.net is used for network communication.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: Java is a high-level, object-oriented programming language designed to be platform independent using the JVM.

interviewQuestions.question: Who developed Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: Java was developed by James Gosling and his team at Sun Microsystems in 1995.

interviewQuestions.question: What are the main features of Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: Java features include platform independence, object-oriented programming, security, robustness, multithreading, and portability.

interviewQuestions.question: What is JVM?
interviewQuestions.answer: JVM stands for Java Virtual Machine. It is responsible for running Java bytecode and enabling platform independence.

interviewQuestions.question: What is JDK?
interviewQuestions.answer: JDK stands for Java Development Kit. It includes tools for developing Java applications such as the compiler and runtime environment.

interviewQuestions.question: What is JRE?
interviewQuestions.answer: JRE stands for Java Runtime Environment. It provides the libraries and JVM required to run Java programs.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between JDK, JRE, and JVM?
interviewQuestions.answer: JDK is used to develop Java applications, JRE provides the runtime environment, and JVM executes Java bytecode.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a class in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: A class is a blueprint used to create objects. It defines properties and behaviors of objects.

interviewQuestions.question: What is an object in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: An object is an instance of a class that contains properties and methods defined in the class.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a constructor?
interviewQuestions.answer: A constructor is a special method used to initialize objects when they are created.

interviewQuestions.question: What are Java data types?
interviewQuestions.answer: Java data types are divided into primitive types like int, float, boolean, char and non-primitive types like String, arrays, and classes.

interviewQuestions.question: What is method overloading?
interviewQuestions.answer: Method overloading allows multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists.

interviewQuestions.question: What is method overriding?
interviewQuestions.answer: Method overriding occurs when a subclass provides a specific implementation of a method already defined in its parent class.

interviewQuestions.question: What is inheritance in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: Inheritance allows a class to inherit properties and methods from another class using the extends keyword.

interviewQuestions.question: What is polymorphism?
interviewQuestions.answer: Polymorphism allows methods to perform different actions depending on the object calling them.

interviewQuestions.question: What is abstraction?
interviewQuestions.answer: Abstraction hides implementation details and shows only essential features to the user.

interviewQuestions.question: What is encapsulation?
interviewQuestions.answer: Encapsulation is the process of wrapping data and methods into a single unit and restricting direct access using access modifiers.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between abstract class and interface?
interviewQuestions.answer: An abstract class can contain both abstract and concrete methods, while an interface contains only abstract methods (before Java 8).

interviewQuestions.question: What is exception handling in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: Exception handling is used to manage runtime errors using try, catch, finally, throw, and throws keywords.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between checked and unchecked exceptions?
interviewQuestions.answer: Checked exceptions are checked at compile time, while unchecked exceptions occur at runtime.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the Java Collections Framework?
interviewQuestions.answer: The Java Collections Framework provides classes and interfaces to store and manipulate groups of objects efficiently.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between ArrayList and LinkedList?
interviewQuestions.answer: ArrayList uses a dynamic array for storage, while LinkedList uses a doubly linked list structure.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a HashMap?
interviewQuestions.answer: HashMap is a collection that stores key-value pairs and allows fast retrieval using keys.

interviewQuestions.question: What is multithreading in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: Multithreading allows multiple threads to execute concurrently within a program.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between process and thread?
interviewQuestions.answer: A process is an independent program in execution, while a thread is a smaller unit of execution within a process.

interviewQuestions.question: What is garbage collection in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: Garbage collection automatically removes unused objects from memory to free up resources.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between == and equals() in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: == compares object references, while equals() compares object values.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a package in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: A package is a namespace that organizes classes and interfaces into groups.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the main method in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: The main method is the entry point of a Java application where execution begins.

interviewQuestions.question: What does the static keyword mean?
interviewQuestions.answer: The static keyword means the member belongs to the class rather than an instance of the class.
